Area Forecast Discussion...CORRECTED
National Weather Service New York NY
357 PM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Low pressure moving up the coast will impact the area with 
rain and some wind Sunday afternoon into Monday morning. Minor 
coastal impacts possible due to approaching full moon on Tuesday.

2) Another coastal storm is possible from Wednesday night into
Thanksgiving Day. More significant coastal flooding could be
possible depending on low track and intensity. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
The 12Z guidance looks fairly similar on the idea of one low 
over central FL remaining weak but a significant rain maker for 
coastal areas from N FL into GA and the Carolinas. A second low 
farther east now looks to become the primary low as it moves N, 
passing the NC Outer Banks early Sunday morning and then over or 
just SE of eastern Long Island late Sunday night. Rain with this 
system could begin as soon as early Sunday afternoon as low level 
ridging erodes and lead low level moisture advection and mid level
shortwave energy aloft ride up the coast. The heaviest rain 
should occur Sunday night west of the low track with the aid of 
strong low level moisture advection east of the center interacting
with mid level frontogenesis NW of the center and large scale 
lift via an upper jet streak to the north. A few elevated tstms 
are also possible with GFS sounding showing some CAPE above 800 mb
in the presence of moist adiabatic lapse rates and deep 
moisture/lift. 

GFS/ECMWF consensus attm is for rainfall to be maximized
somewhere across Long Island/southern CT and possibly NYC, where
a stripe of close to 3 inches may be possible, with amts 1-2 
inches outside of that across the CWA. Max rainfall rates in
this heavier stripe could run over 1/2 inch per hour for 
several hours. The flash flood risk still appears marginal, 
since the quick hitting nature of this system and its timing 
suggest more of an urban/small stream/poor drainage minor flood 
threat. 

The above impacts appear likely to occur regardless of any
subtropical or tropical development of this system per NHC. 
This makes sense with FSU phase diagrams showing the sys 
evolving into more of an asymmetric/shallow warm core system
with latitude as it moves over much colder waters N of the Gulf
Stream, with the warm core intensifying via the baroclinic (non-
tropical) processes outlined above. 

Wind impact Sunday night will depend on the track of the sfc 
low. If the low center moves across Long Island per some ECMWF 
ensemble members, eastern Long Island and SE CT could see a 
period of strong SE-S winds meeting at least advisory criteria 
with gusts 45-55 mph. A few northerly gusts up to 40 mph may 
also be possible west of the low center as it passes by. 

The coastal flood threat appears minimal as high tide occurs Mon
AM after passage of the low center, with winds offshore but
elevated offshore seas hindering drainage out of the back bays.
A few Long Island south shore locations may approach or touch 
minor thresholds during that time. 

.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Models agree on potential for another coastal storm Wed night
into Thanksgiving Day. Deterministic ECMWF tracks the low SE of
Nantucket Thanksgiving night, with the GFS even farther 
offshore. Wind pacts would be more limited to ern Long Island/CT
under that scenario. However, tracks of stronger ensemble 
solutions are mostly NW of that, with more direct impact to the 
CWA, and a more widespread wind threat to coastal sections, as 
well as a greater coastal flood threat. STOFS 12Z guidance 
(based off 06Z GFS with its stronger low/winds near the coast) 
plus 1/2 foot (a good long range proxy) suggests reasonable 
worst case potential for moderate flooding over multiple high 
tide cycles Wed into Fri. At least widespread minor coastal
flooding possible even with more offshore solutions, with this
storm occurring right after the full moon. 

&&

.AVIATION /19Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
High pressure remains in control through the TAF period. 

VFR. 

Wind direction varies for the next few hours from SW to WNW and
under 10 kt. Becoming closer to 5 kt or less approaching 00z. 
Most non-city terminal winds go calm by or shortly after 00z. 
Light winds remain into Saturday morning with a light onshore 
wind developing towards midday. 

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

No unscheduled amendments expected.

.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z Saturday through Wednesday... 

Saturday afternoon: VFR. Winds become more E to SE and mainly
under 10 kt. 

Sunday: Chance of MVFR or lower conditions developing in RA. Sub
VFR in RA at night.

Monday: MVFR or lower likely early in RA, improvement likely in
PM. NW-W wind G20-25kt. 

Tuesday: VFR. Weakening NW-N flow. 

Wednesday: VFR. Sub VFR possible at night. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Low pressure moving up the coast will produce at least SCA cond
on all waters Sunday night, lingering thereafter on the ocean as
winds ands seas remain elevated in NW flow after low passage and
cold air advection. Depending on low track there is a chance for
gales on the ocean waters and the ern Sound/bays Sunday night.
Too early to issue a gale watch but one may become necessary if
confidence in low track increases. 

Gales may be possible on all waters Wed night with the area
sandwiched between an approaching coastal storm and strong high
pressure to the north.
